summary: Fast path waits for the 60 s guarded operator entry instead of abandoning it at 30-38 s
reason: File37 O6: the fast path must not give up while the network guard holds Wi-Fi off. Guard bound 60 s (decision of 11/10 on fixtures/s24-2026-10-11/o6-network-guard-timing.json); helper waits 70 s, Node and gemini processes allow it.

tests.name: o6-guarded-wait-python
tests.evidence: test-guarded-operator-wait.py: 5 tests on the captured 10/10 09:41 resolution; guarded entry raises only the read execution wait to 70 s, ordinary routes keep 30 s, the confirmed handoff budget is untouched, gemini process timeout 90 s.

tests.name: o6-guarded-wait-node
tests.evidence: test-guarded-entry-wait.cjs: executing calls are killed only after 85 s (30 s owner inbound) or the caller budget + 15 s; check-only calls keep timeout + 8 s.

capabilities.reason: No route or action change; existing telecom.orange.consultation keeps its entry, only the wait is aligned (documented in the registry by playbooks #57).

architecture.reason: Timeout alignment in the existing fast path; no store, router, scheduler or daemon.

rollback: Revert this PR; the fast path returns to its 30 s / 38 s waits.
limitations: The 60 s bound itself lives in the guard (core #112, O1); before #112 is deployed the guard child has no bound and this wait is only an upper limit of the caller.
Live recipe by Claude with O1/O3: a guarded consultation finishes inside the bound with network_guard.restored true.
